post_text:
Anthropic had three significant moves this week. None were officially announced.

1. Claude Builder leaked on X. Screenshots show a "build mode" built directly into Claude's UI, taglined "Let's ship something great." It includes quick-start app templates, a live preview panel, built-in security scanning, and options to explore design directions or implement dark mode. Full-stack app generation inside Claude itself. Lovable and Bolt are now competing with the model provider.

2. Claude Code is getting a multi-repo interface. Leaked screenshots show split view, a task panel, and parallel agent execution across repositories in one unified workspace. This is a significant upgrade from the current single-repo model.

3. Claude Opus 4.6 dropped 15 percentage points on Bridge Bench. It went from 83.3% to 68.3% accuracy on hallucination detection — rank 2 down to rank 10. Anthropic said nothing publicly. Three credible theories: a silent weight update, compute being reallocated toward Opus 4.7 (spotted in an internal API endpoint), or intentional softening ahead of a Metis launch.

On the benchmark side: Metis leads GPT-5.4 Pro on SWE-bench coding (93.9 vs 80.0), HLE reasoning (56.8 vs 42.7), and Graph Walks long-context tasks (80.0 vs 21.4). GPT leads on Browser CoP (89.3 vs 86.9). Metis is also priced lower — $25/$125 vs $30/$180 per million tokens.

Three coordinated moves in one week. Whether the Opus nerf is intentional or not, the pattern is clear: Anthropic is repositioning across the stack simultaneously.

Worth watching closely.
idea_title: Anthropic LEAKED: NEW Claude Builder, Mythos Benchmarks & Opus 4.6 NERFED!
